Open ruling: A day that carries a block runs to about 360 taught minutes against the 300-minute ceiling, so either the campus day runs full on those days or the trainer's agenda gives up 60 minutes, starting from its cut-first line.

## Cross-check against the tracker

Every session sits on the same day in the faculty workbook and in the tracker's violet column, each on a teaching day inside its own week, and the per-week counts match the 20-Week Plan.

## Per session

### W2-1 · Mon 12 Oct 2026 · Sampling distributions and the central limit theorem

Day: W02/D1. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 1: Foundations of AI and Data. Subject: Statistical inference.

Learning outcomes: Learners can define a standard error, explain why sample means are approximately normal, and explain why an estimate from a very small sample is unreliable.

Prior coverage: Week 1: descriptive statistics in Python; a permutation test run by hand and then in code with 5,000 label shuffles; the p-value stated as the share of chance-only outcomes at least as extreme as the observed one; the confidence interval named and never constructed. No formula-based inference has been taught.

Reserved for later: Confidence intervals and the t-test family (W2-2); power, sample size and multiple comparisons (W2-3).

### W2-2 · Tue 13 Oct 2026 · Confidence intervals and the t-test family

Day: W02/D2. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 1: Foundations of AI and Data. Subject: Statistical inference.

Learning outcomes: Learners can construct and interpret a 95 percent confidence interval, select an appropriate test for a given comparison, and explain what an interval adds to a p-value.

Prior coverage: W2-1: sampling distributions, the standard error and the central limit theorem. From Week 1: the permutation test and the meaning of a p-value.

Reserved for later: Power, sample size and multiple comparisons (W2-3); inference on regression coefficients (W5-1).

### W2-3 · Wed 14 Oct 2026 · Errors, power and sample size; multiple comparisons

Day: W02/D3. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 1: Foundations of AI and Data. Subject: Statistical inference.

Learning outcomes: Learners can estimate the sample size a comparison needs, explain why testing many segments produces spurious findings, and distinguish a statistically significant result from a practically important one.

Prior coverage: W2-1 and W2-2. From Week 1: correlation against causation, confounding and Simpson's paradox, taught on a marketing campaign dataset; a working rule that a rate computed on fewer than thirty observations is unreliable.

Reserved for later: Experiment design and A/B testing (W4-1); regression (Week 5).

### W4-1 · Mon 26 Oct 2026 · Design of experiments: randomised controlled trials and A/B testing

Day: W04/D1. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 2: Applied Machine Learning. Subject: Experimentation and causal measurement.

Learning outcomes: Learners can design an A/B test for a product change, specifying the unit randomised, the primary and guardrail metrics, the sample size and the duration, and can name two ways such a test goes wrong.

Prior coverage: Applied session: a north-star metric with guardrail metrics, leading against lagging indicators, metric definitions with numerator, denominator and window, and how a target gets gamed. Weeks 1 and 2: the permutation test, t-tests, power, sample size and confounding.

Reserved for later: Classification metrics and prediction (Week 5). Causal inference from observational data, beyond confounding, is outside the programme.

### W4-2 · Wed 28 Oct 2026 · Association rule mining: probability foundations and the Apriori algorithm

Day: W04/D3. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 2: Applied Machine Learning. Subject: Association analysis.

Learning outcomes: Learners can derive lift from a contingency table, explain how frequent itemsets are found without enumerating every combination, and state why high confidence alone is misleading.

Prior coverage: Applied session: support, confidence and lift computed by counting on twelve baskets and then in code; a best-selling item with confidence 0.82 and lift 0.97, recognised as uninformative; one recommendation costed as expected incremental margin less promotion cost.

Reserved for later: Recommender systems and collaborative filtering are outside the programme.

### W4-3 · Thu 29 Oct 2026 · Time-to-event analysis: survival curves, censoring and hazard

Day: W04/D4. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 2: Applied Machine Learning. Subject: Survival and retention analysis.

Learning outcomes: Learners can read a Kaplan-Meier curve, explain censoring and its effect on a retention estimate, and state when two retention curves differ by more than chance.

Prior coverage: Applied session: cohorts built by signup month; funnels read with the correct denominator at each stage; retention curves; a blended retention rate that stays flat while every cohort declines, which is a mix effect related to the Simpson's paradox example of Week 1.

Reserved for later: Predictive churn models (Week 5). Customer lifetime value modelling is outside the programme.

### W4-4 · Fri 30 Oct 2026 · Time series foundations: autocorrelation, stationarity, exponential smoothing and ARIMA

Day: W04/D5. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 2: Applied Machine Learning. Subject: Time series and forecasting.

Learning outcomes: Learners can read an autocorrelation plot, explain exponential smoothing as a weighted memory of the past, and state what a fitted model must beat before it is preferred to a seasonal-naive forecast.

Prior coverage: Applied session: trend and seasonality read from 24 months of revenue with an annual festival peak; last-value, seasonal-naive and drift forecasts built by hand; a six-month hold-out scored with mean absolute error; a vendor forecast that lost to the seasonal-naive baseline.

Reserved for later: Machine-learning and neural forecasting methods are outside the programme.

### W5-1 · Mon 02 Nov 2026 · Linear and logistic regression from first principles

Day: W05/D1. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 2: Applied Machine Learning. Subject: Supervised learning: linear models.

Learning outcomes: Learners can explain where least-squares and logistic-regression estimates come from, interpret a coefficient together with its standard error, and state the assumptions behind the inference.

Prior coverage: Applied session: a prediction problem framed as input, target and prediction time; train, validation and test splits; a naive baseline; linear and logistic regression fitted in scikit-learn, with coefficients interpreted in business units and residual plots examined. A pre-work bridge course introduced both models. Week 2: intervals and t-tests.

Reserved for later: Evaluation metrics (W5-2); multicollinearity (W5-3); regularisation (W5-4).

### W5-2 · Tue 03 Nov 2026 · Classifier evaluation: ROC analysis, precision-recall and cost-sensitive decisions

Day: W05/D2. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 2: Applied Machine Learning. Subject: Model evaluation.

Learning outcomes: Learners can read ROC and precision-recall curves, derive a decision threshold from two misclassification costs, and explain why a model that ranks well can still be poorly calibrated.

Prior coverage: Applied session: the confusion matrix, precision, recall and F1; a classifier that is 96 percent accurate on a 96-to-4 outcome and identifies no positives; metric selection from the cost of each error type; a threshold chosen from two costs in a retail case, and again in a lending case where the costs reverse. ROC and AUC were named only.

Reserved for later: Statistical comparison of models on a shared test set (W10-3).

### W5-3 · Wed 04 Nov 2026 · Multicollinearity, identifiability, and explanatory against predictive modelling

Day: W05/D3. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 2: Applied Machine Learning. Subject: Model specification and feature engineering.

Learning outcomes: Learners can diagnose multicollinearity with a variance inflation factor, explain why a coefficient changed sign, and state when a model is fit to explain and when it is fit only to predict.

Prior coverage: Applied session: recency, frequency and monetary features, ratios, encoding and scaling; leakage detected by asking whether a value is known at prediction time; two correlated features that reversed a coefficient's sign in the learners' own model.

Reserved for later: Regularisation as the remedy for unstable coefficients (W5-4).

### W5-4 · Thu 05 Nov 2026 · The bias-variance trade-off, regularisation and resampling

Day: W05/D4. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 2: Applied Machine Learning. Subject: Generalisation and regularisation.

Learning outcomes: Learners can explain the bias-variance decomposition, state what ridge and lasso penalties do to the coefficients and why, and describe how cross-validation estimates generalisation error without touching the test set.

Prior coverage: Applied session: an unrestricted decision tree scoring 100 percent on training data and 61 percent on validation data; learning curves; regularisation strength and k-fold cross-validation used in scikit-learn; trees, ensembles and clustering met at recognition depth.

Reserved for later: The internals of trees and ensembles (W5-5); regularisation in neural networks (W7-3).

### W5-5 · Fri 06 Nov 2026 · Decision trees, bagging, random forests and gradient boosting

Day: W05/D5. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 2: Applied Machine Learning. Subject: Tree-based and ensemble methods.

Learning outcomes: Learners can compute one split by hand, explain why averaging many trees lowers variance, and describe what each boosting iteration fits.

Prior coverage: Applied session: a model justification memo in which the simpler model is recommended when performance ties, the cost of errors is stated in currency and a retraining rule is set. Decision trees, random forests and gradient boosting were used in scikit-learn on Thursday without examining their internals.

Reserved for later: Neural networks (Week 7).

### W7-1 · Mon 16 Nov 2026 · Feed-forward networks: representation, non-linearity and depth

Day: W07/D1. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 3: Deep Learning and Neural Networks. Subject: Neural network fundamentals.

Learning outcomes: Learners can explain why a network needs non-linear activations, state the universal approximation theorem and its limits, and relate a single neuron to logistic regression.

Prior coverage: Applied session: the neuron; a forward pass traced by hand on two neurons; sigmoid, tanh and ReLU compared on one input range; the collapse of stacked layers when the activation is removed; a small network that only matches logistic regression on tabular data. Week 5: logistic regression and regularisation.

Reserved for later: Backpropagation and optimisers (W7-2); initialisation and normalisation (W7-3). Convolutional networks are outside the programme.

### W7-2 · Tue 17 Nov 2026 · Backpropagation derived, and gradient-based optimisation

Day: W07/D2. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 3: Deep Learning and Neural Networks. Subject: Optimisation and backpropagation.

Learning outcomes: Learners can derive the gradients of a two-layer network by hand, explain what reverse-mode automatic differentiation computes, and state what momentum and Adam each change about plain gradient descent.

Prior coverage: Applied session: loss functions for regression and classification; backpropagation explained as error attribution, with one weight updated by hand from a given gradient; SGD, momentum, RMSProp and Adam at recognition depth; the effect of the learning rate; a training run that diverged to NaN.

Reserved for later: Vanishing and exploding gradients, initialisation and normalisation (W7-3).

### W7-3 · Wed 18 Nov 2026 · Vanishing and exploding gradients, initialisation, normalisation and regularisation in deep networks

Day: W07/D3. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 3: Deep Learning and Neural Networks. Subject: Training dynamics and regularisation.

Learning outcomes: Learners can explain why deep sigmoid networks train slowly, give the variance argument behind Xavier and He initialisation, and state what batch normalisation, dropout and weight decay each do.

Prior coverage: Applied session: loss curves read as a diagnostic vocabulary; vanishing and exploding gradients at intuition depth; three faulty training runs diagnosed from their curves; regularisation, dropout, early stopping and random seeds applied as remedies. W5-4: ridge and lasso.

Reserved for later: Recurrent networks (W7-4), where the same gradient problem reappears through time.

### W7-4 · Thu 19 Nov 2026 · Recurrent networks, LSTM and the path to attention

Day: W07/D4. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 3: Deep Learning and Neural Networks. Subject: Sequence models.

Learning outcomes: Learners can unroll a recurrent network, explain how LSTM gating eases the vanishing-gradient problem, and state the bottleneck that attention was introduced to remove.

Prior coverage: Applied session: text as token ids and vectors; recurrent, LSTM (GRU named), bidirectional and encoder-decoder families placed on one map; next-token prediction and auto-regression with a small character-level model; the long-range dependency failure, and why attention replaced recurrence, at intuition depth.

Reserved for later: Self-attention and the transformer (W8-1).

### W7-5 · Fri 20 Nov 2026 · Subword tokenization and the evaluation of language models

Day: W07/D5. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 4: Natural Language Processing. Subject: Tokenization and statistical language modelling.

Learning outcomes: Learners can run byte-pair encoding merges by hand, compute perplexity from token probabilities, and explain why two models' perplexities cannot be compared when their tokenizers differ.

Prior coverage: Applied session: why models read tokens and not words; what byte-pair encoding optimises; token counts as a cost driver, with one day of customer-support tickets costed; BPE, WordPiece and SentencePiece named; a product code that fragments into five tokens. W7-4: next-token prediction.

Reserved for later: Attention and the transformer (W8-1); embeddings (W8-2).

### W8-1 · Mon 23 Nov 2026 · Scaled dot-product attention and the transformer block

Day: W08/D1. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 4: Natural Language Processing. Subject: Attention and the transformer architecture.

Learning outcomes: Learners can write scaled dot-product attention as matrix operations, justify the scaling factor, and state the time and memory cost of self-attention in sequence length.

Prior coverage: Applied session: attention explained as every token consulting every other token; queries, keys and values; one attention step computed by hand on three tokens; multi-head attention and positional information introduced; the transformer of Vaswani et al. (2017) with six layers, eight heads and model width 512. W7-4: the encoder-decoder bottleneck and additive attention.

Reserved for later: Positional encodings and long contexts (W8-4); key-value cache memory (W10-4).

### W8-2 · Wed 25 Nov 2026 · Word and sentence embeddings: how they are learned and what their geometry means

Day: W08/D3. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 4: Natural Language Processing. Subject: Representation learning for text.

Learning outcomes: Learners can explain the skip-gram objective, distinguish static from contextual embeddings, and explain how a sentence-embedding model is trained and why a high cosine similarity can still mislead.

Prior coverage: Applied session: the progression from TF-IDF and static word vectors to contextual embeddings; BERT as an encoder and GPT as a decoder, and the tasks each suits; a similar-ticket search in which a neighbour with cosine similarity 0.91 was not relevant.

Reserved for later: Retrieval, indexing and ranking (Week 11).

### W8-3 · Thu 26 Nov 2026 · Decoding as search: from beam search to sampling methods

Day: W08/D4. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 4: Natural Language Processing. Subject: Text generation and decoding.

Learning outcomes: Learners can explain why beam search yields repetitive output in open-ended generation, state what temperature, top-k and top-p each do to the next-token distribution, and choose a decoding strategy for a given task.

Prior coverage: Applied session: greedy decoding against sampling; temperature, top-k and top-p adjusted live on one customer-support ticket; stop conditions and determinism; an unterminated generation and its cost.

Reserved for later: Constrained and grammar-guided decoding (W10-2).

### W8-4 · Fri 27 Nov 2026 · Positional encodings, long-context attention and scaling laws

Day: W08/D5. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 4: Natural Language Processing. Subject: Position, long context and scaling.

Learning outcomes: Learners can explain how position enters a transformer, why doubling the context more than doubles the computation, and what a scaling law predicts and does not predict.

Prior coverage: Applied session: the context window as a fixed budget, and what is lost when it overflows; input and output tokens priced differently; prefill against decode, time to first token and the key-value cache named; batching; a cost model for two thousand support tickets a day. W8-1: the cost of attention.

Reserved for later: Key-value cache memory, batching arithmetic and quantisation (W10-4); the lost-in-the-middle effect (W11-5).

### W10-1 · Mon 07 Dec 2026 · From pretraining to instruction following: instruction tuning, preference optimisation and in-context learning

Day: W10/D1. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 5: Generative AI Foundations. Subject: Alignment and in-context learning.

Learning outcomes: Learners can describe the training stages that produce an instruction-following model, explain why few-shot examples change behaviour without any weight update, and name two known sensitivities of few-shot prompting.

Prior coverage: Applied session: zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought and task decomposition compared on forty labelled support tickets with a single score; the role of a system prompt; a few-shot example set that biased every prediction toward one category. Week 8: transformer internals and decoding.

Reserved for later: Evaluation statistics (W10-3). Parameter-efficient fine-tuning is not part of this session.

### W10-2 · Tue 08 Dec 2026 · Constrained decoding: formal grammars, automata and token masking

Day: W10/D2. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 5: Generative AI Foundations. Subject: Structured and constrained generation.

Learning outcomes: Learners can explain how a schema becomes a token mask at each decoding step, and distinguish what constrained decoding guarantees (well-formed output) from what still requires validation (correct content).

Prior coverage: Applied session: an output contract defined as a schema, a validator and a failure policy; JSON Schema and typed data models; a bounded repair loop; a provider's structured-output mode enabled and its guarantees noted.

Reserved for later: Function calling and tool use are taught by the industry trainer on Wednesday.

### W10-3 · Thu 10 Dec 2026 · The statistics of model evaluation: sample size, agreement and significance

Day: W10/D4. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 5: Generative AI Foundations. Subject: Evaluation methodology.

Learning outcomes: Learners can attach a confidence interval to an evaluation score, test whether two prompt or model versions differ on a shared test set, and compute and interpret Cohen's kappa between a model judge and a human annotator.

Prior coverage: Applied session: a golden test set and a rubric of binary checks; programmatic checks, human labels and a model as judge, applied in that order; judge bias by answer length and by position demonstrated; a regression run across three prompt versions. Week 2: intervals, tests, power and multiple comparisons.

Reserved for later: Ranking metrics such as nDCG (W11-4).

### W10-4 · Fri 11 Dec 2026 · The arithmetic of LLM inference: memory, throughput and quantisation

Day: W10/D5. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 5: Generative AI Foundations. Subject: Inference efficiency.

Learning outcomes: Learners can estimate the key-value cache memory for a given model and context length, explain why decoding is limited by memory bandwidth, and describe the trade-off between latency and throughput under batching.

Prior coverage: Applied session: cost per request, time to first token and total latency measured; the prompt shortened and its prefix cached; simple requests routed to a smaller model with a quality check on that slice; streaming. W8-4: the key-value cache named, and the quadratic cost of attention.

Reserved for later: Model serving and deployment (Week 14, industry practitioners).

### W11-1 · Mon 14 Dec 2026 · Classical information retrieval: the vector space model, TF-IDF and BM25

Day: W11/D1. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 6: Applied Generative AI. Subject: Information retrieval: classical models.

Learning outcomes: Learners can compute TF-IDF and BM25 scores by hand for a small collection, explain what the k1 and b parameters control, and state when lexical retrieval outperforms dense retrieval.

Prior coverage: Applied session: a minimal retrieval-augmented pipeline built end to end (split, embed, store, retrieve, generate from the retrieved evidence only); chunk size, overlap and structure-aware splitting compared on ten questions. Week 8: TF-IDF recalled; embeddings (W8-2).

Reserved for later: Approximate nearest-neighbour search (W11-2); rank fusion and learning to rank (W11-3); evaluation metrics (W11-4).

### W11-2 · Tue 15 Dec 2026 · Approximate nearest-neighbour search: LSH, product quantisation and HNSW

Day: W11/D2. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 6: Applied Generative AI. Subject: Vector search and indexing.

Learning outcomes: Learners can explain why approximate search trades recall for speed, describe how HNSW and product quantisation work, and tune an index parameter against a recall target.

Prior coverage: Applied session: an embedding model selected on the organisation's own questions, including mixed-language queries; a vector index in PostgreSQL (pgvector) with exact and approximate search compared as a setting; metadata filtering; index refresh when documents change. W8-2: embeddings and cosine similarity.

Reserved for later: Hybrid retrieval, rank fusion and reranking (W11-3).

### W11-3 · Wed 16 Dec 2026 · Learning to rank, neural rerankers and rank fusion

Day: W11/D3. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 6: Applied Generative AI. Subject: Ranking and fusion.

Learning outcomes: Learners can explain why a cross-encoder ranks more accurately than a bi-encoder and costs more, distinguish pointwise, pairwise and listwise training, and compute a reciprocal rank fusion by hand.

Prior coverage: Applied session: BM25 keyword search run beside vector search; reciprocal rank fusion computed by hand and in code; a reranker reducing fifty candidates to five, with its latency measured; query rewriting for follow-up questions. W11-1 and W11-2.

Reserved for later: nDCG and significance testing (W11-4).

### W11-4 · Thu 17 Dec 2026 · Evaluating retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation

Day: W11/D4. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 6: Applied Generative AI. Subject: Retrieval and RAG evaluation.

Learning outcomes: Learners can compute nDCG and MRR by hand, test whether an improvement across a query set exceeds chance, and separate a retrieval failure from a generation failure.

Prior coverage: Applied session: a retrieval test set that includes unanswerable questions; recall at k, precision at k and reciprocal rank computed by hand and in code; faithfulness and relevance graded; each failure attributed to retrieval or to generation. W10-3: intervals, paired tests and agreement.

Reserved for later: Long-context behaviour and hallucination (W11-5).

### W11-5 · Fri 18 Dec 2026 · Long-context behaviour, grounding and hallucination in language models

Day: W11/D5. Status: Tentative. Faculty: to be confirmed by IIT Gandhinagar. Module 6: Applied Generative AI. Subject: Grounding, long context and hallucination.

Learning outcomes: Learners can state the lost-in-the-middle finding and one proposed mechanism, classify a hallucination by type, and explain why a model's stated confidence is a weak guide to its factual accuracy.

Prior coverage: Applied session: citations checked programmatically; abstaining when the retrieved evidence is insufficient; two source documents that conflict; an entire policy document placed in a long context as a costed alternative to retrieval, with weaker use of mid-context information observed. W8-4: context windows and the cost of attention.

Reserved for later: Agentic systems, tool use and multi-agent design (Weeks 13 to 15, industry practitioners).
